comparison: Both evaluations support KDM2B's DNA binding specificity (C3, C28, C29). OpenEval focuses on EMSA evidence for non-methylated DNA recognition, while peer reviewers accepted the DNA binding data without challenge, focusing instead on interpretation questions.

Both support genome-wide CGI localization (C30, C31, C32). OpenEval cites ChIP-seq and Bio-CAP-seq correlation as strong evidence, while peer reviewers accepted these findings as part of the overall DNA binding characterization.

Disagreement on KDM2B's preferential association with polycomb targets (C35, C36, C37). OpenEval finds MA-plot and GO term analysis provide consistent support, while peer reviewers question the mechanism, asking 'What excludes KDM2A from Polycomb target CGIs?'

Both support complex composition findings (C38, C39, C40, C55). OpenEval emphasizes mass spectrometry and co-IP validation, while peer reviewers accepted the data but requested clarification about interaction domains and CBX-containing complex exclusion.

Both support DNA-binding domain requirement (C41, C42). OpenEval cites loss-of-function experiments in RING1B knockout and ZF-CxxC mutant cells, while peer reviewers accepted this finding as part of the DNA binding characterization.

Disagreement on gene repression claims (C43, C44, C45). OpenEval finds western blot and microarray data supportive, while peer reviewers question functional significance, noting that 'loss of KDM2B only derepresses a very small subset' despite affecting all RING1B sites.

Disagreement on PRC1 recruitment role (C4, C46, C47, C48, C49). OpenEval finds ChIP-seq evidence of genome-wide RING1B reduction compelling, while peer reviewers note 'Only a small subset of KDM2B binding sites are also occupied by RING1B so other features or factors must be involved.'

Disagreement on H2AK119ub1 regulation (C5, C50, C51, C52, C53). OpenEval finds western blot and ChIP-qPCR evidence sufficient, while peer reviewers express concern about magnitude, noting 'in most cases it is no more than 20% lower' and suggesting 'KDM2B plays a minor role.'

Both support widespread low-level RING1B occupancy (C6, C59, C60). OpenEval emphasizes ChIP-seq and expression data supporting the sampling model, while peer reviewers acknowledged this 'surprising observation' without challenging the data.

Disagreement on mechanistic conclusions (C54, C56). OpenEval finds converging evidence supports the DNA-binding recruitment model, while peer reviewers state 'Without a mechanism to recruit PRC2 to the same sites, the model is not very explanatory' and note 'several links missing in the causal chain.'

Opposite assessments of sampling model speculation (C7, C57, C58). OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN noting these are 'explicitly speculative interpretations,' while peer reviewers did not challenge the hypothesis and accepted the manuscript with this model included.

Both agree on uncertainty regarding PRC2 recruitment models (C63, C64, C65). OpenEval notes these are 'explicitly speculative models' lacking validation, while peer reviewers ask 'How is PRC2 recruited to KDM2B/RING1B sites?' indicating the mechanism remains unclear.

Peer reviewers explicitly challenged the assumption about PRC1 binding automatically compacting chromatin (C24), stating this is 'misguided' given bivalent sites in ES cells. No corresponding OpenEval evaluation found for this claim.

Peer reviewers questioned the functional relevance of H3K36 demethylase activity at CGIs (C16, C17), asking 'What are H3K36 demethylases doing at sites not expected to contain H3K36 methylation?' No corresponding OpenEval evaluation found.
